A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same ODR likelihood and consistency framework by the same authors. Their main texts, mathematical material, displays, and complete appendices support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 Section 6 and Table 3 report original Robosuite Panda-Lift experiments comparing fitted mass distributions and estimation errors for DROPO and E-DROPO.

after.justification: V2 contains theoretical results and a conceptual diagram, but no original empirical outcomes in its main text or appendices. The earlier experiments are removed.

M1.justification: V2 removes E-DROPO, including its entropy-augmented likelihood objective in v1 Section 5.2 and its procedure in Appendix E. The underlying Gaussian maximum-likelihood ODR formulation remains.

E1.justification: V2 removes the sole evaluated setting: estimating four body masses from offline trajectories in Robosuite Panda-Lift. No replacement dataset, task, or empirical test scenario is introduced.

E2.justification: V1 Table 3 evaluates original DROPO against E-DROPO; v2 removes this entire comparison. Continued citations to DROPO, DROID, and BayesSim describe prior work rather than retained evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The empirical protocol disappears: 20 or 40 offline trajectories, bounded four-mass searches, 20 CMA-ES iterations with 10 simulator samples per iteration, and mean-estimation L2 error labeled MSE. V2 introduces no empirical evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: V1 provides a limited check of entropy regularization's proposed effect on covariance collapse by comparing fitted spreads and estimation errors against unregularized DROPO at two data budgets. V2 removes this check and adds no empirical ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The sigma entries in v1 Table 3 describe fitted Gaussian distributions, not uncertainty across experimental runs.

E6.justification: All empirical result entries disappear. V1 Table 3 reports DROPO/E-DROPO errors of 6.19/1.44 for 20 trajectories and 3.35/2.28 for 40 trajectories, alongside fitted means and standard deviations; none is retained or replaced in v2.

T1.justification: V2 makes Assumption 4 explicitly depend on dataset coverage and adds identified-set consistency, upper hemicontinuity, and representative-MDP value-perturbation/misspecification results in Section 6.4 and Appendix D.3-D.4. It removes v1 Appendix D's comparative ODR transfer bounds and Appendix A.3's entropy derivation. The weak/strong consistency results remain; the positivity-tail relaxation and Lipschitz sufficient condition already existed in v1 Appendices A.5 and A.4 and are largely relocated.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion shift from consistency plus O(M)-tighter transfer bounds and a new entropy-regularized algorithm to statistical consistency and the practicality and relaxation of its assumptions. E-DROPO's advertised robust-transfer contribution is withdrawn.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive discussion of dependent data, coverage-dependent identification, observationally indistinguishable parameters, limitations on quantifying identified-set size, and misspecification error. Appendix D.2 also distinguishes smoothness in physical parameters from contact-related nonsmoothness in states and actions. The earlier entropy-collapse mechanism and comparative transfer-bound interpretations disappear.

D1.justification: V2 removes the implementation information in v1 Section 6, Table 2, and Appendix E: mass bounds, beta = 0.002, variance regularization of 10^-5, CMA-ES settings, simulator reset/sampling instructions, and the sampled-next-state Gaussian likelihood construction. No replacement implementation or reproducibility information is supplied.

R1.justification: The advertised relationship to prior work changes substantially: v1 proposes an extension of Tiboni et al.'s DROPO and improved guarantees relative to Chen et al.; v2 centers consistency and assumption relaxations instead. Although Section 2 is largely retained, Berge (1963) is added, while Agrawal and Jia, Auer et al., Fruit et al., Kwon et al., and the Robosuite reference are removed with the dropped material.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, contributions, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Section 5 is reorganized, experimental Section 6 is replaced by an assumptions discussion, and existing relaxation proofs move from Appendix A into the reorganized Appendix D. These changes substantially alter the narrative structure.

P2.justification: V2 removes all three v1 tables and the Algorithm 1 display, and adds Figure 1 illustrating uniform versus offline domain randomization. It also adopts ICLR formatting with recurring conference headers and revised title, author, and section typography.

improvement.justification: V2 makes coverage requirements explicit, adds useful partial-identification results, and withdraws robust-transfer claims that v1 supported only with mass-estimation experiments. However, new Section 6.1 overstates what fixed behavior policies guarantee about independence, stationarity, and ergodicity. Appendix D.4 also identifies averaged-kernel training with episode-level domain randomization without establishing their equivalence. These gains and new problems in the applicability arguments leave the net direction of overall quality uncertain.
